children: Earnings season gathered momentum during the last week, with 76 S&P 500 companies reporting results across key sectors, including Financials, Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary, Industrials, and Energy.
The results offered a fresh look at corporate earnings growth and revenue trends across banking, consumer spending, industrial activity, and energy markets.
Of the 76 companies reporting, 62 firms (~82%) exceeded EPS expectations, while 10 fell short and 4 matched estimates. Notably, 60 firms (~79%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.
Of the 76 companies reporting, 48 firms (63%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 28 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 64 firms (~84%) posted Y/Y revenue growth.
Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

— Adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.45 consensus, and revenue of $28.05B edged past estimates despite being flat Y/Y. Free cash flow rebounded to $1.53B, while capital spending reached $4.7B; the company lowered its 2026 capex forecast to $20B from $25B.

— Revenue jumped 26% Y/Y to $64.6B, beating estimates, while adjusted EPS was $7.40 excluding a $9.89B legal charge. Meta forecast Q4 revenue of $73B–$76B and 2026 capex of $135B–$145B as AI spending remains a central focus.

— Revenue and adjusted EPS beat expectations, with free cash flow at $5.0B and adjusted EBITDA up 5.4% Y/Y to $12.5B. Postpaid phone additions missed expectations; AT&T raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to around $2.40.

— EPS of $0.87 beat consensus by $0.05, but revenue of $12.87B narrowly missed estimates despite 12% Y/Y growth. Netflix lowered its 2026 advertising revenue target to $2.7B from about $3B, citing a slower rollout of ad-product capabilities.

— Adjusted EPS of $2.25 beat estimates by $0.23, while adjusted revenue of $13.29B topped consensus by $407M. Orders surged 49% to $19B, and GE raised its 2026 outlook, supported by demand for engines and commercial services.
— EPS of $2.95 beat the $2.88 consensus, while revenue of $17.1B topped estimates of $16.87B. IBM maintained its 2026 revenue-growth outlook of 4%–5%; software and infrastructure both beat consensus.

— Fiscal Q1 2027 sales rose 4% Y/Y to $23.3B, while core EPS increased 1% to $2.00. P&G maintained its full-year organic sales and core EPS growth outlook but raised its estimated after-tax cost headwind to $1.4B.

— Q3 sales increased 11% Y/Y to $20.7B, while diluted EPS rose to $7.97 from $6.95. The company raised its 2026 outlook for the second consecutive quarter and reported a record $292B backlog, including $52.5B tied to a multiyear PAC-3 missile interceptor award.

— Adjusted EPS of $2.26 beat consensus by $0.48, while revenue of $24.97B topped estimates by about $860M. RTX raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $7.65–$7.75 and free cash flow guidance to $9.0B–$9.2B; its backlog reached a record $340B.

— Adjusted EPS of $3.70 beat the $3.57 consensus, while revenue rose 2.9% Y/Y to $50.02B, topping estimates. GM narrowed its 2026 adjusted EBIT outlook to $14.5B–$15.5B and announced a new $20B share-repurchase program.
Earnings season accelerates next week, with mega-cap technology leaders Microsoft
are also due to report, alongside financial firms American Express
